design.concept: A two-step, one-handed flow for the finance person on a phone. Step one is the queue of approved expenses, stacked as large touch rows with amount on the right and a category filter on top. Step two opens after a tap: the expense data is shown for checking and, right below, the payment date and one clear button to register the payment.

views.purpose: Queue of approved expenses waiting for payment: category filter with removable token, tappable rows (category, collaborator, date, amount), load more. Failure, loading and empty states appear in the list's own region.

Check the chosen expense (card with amount, category, collaborator, date, description, status) and register the payment date. Back returns to the queue; after success the expense has left the queue and the person goes back to it.

design.decisions: Used the scene host in scenary mode: queue and payment are steps of one job, so a single narrow column shows one thing at a time and the back control keeps the place. The record list is the preferred molecule with two rich cells (identity stack and right-aligned amount) so rows are readable at 360px and the amount follows the ledger rule: last, right-aligned, tabular figures. The search bar filters by category (a declared query input); colaboradorId is shown as a removable token only if already set, and never typed. No totals or counts are shown because the contract delivers none and the page must not compute them. Paging uses a 'load more' button (the contract exposes hasMore, not a page count), so the pagination control is not used. The payment date uses the shortcut picker (today/yesterday are the usual cases); the confirm button is disabled until a date exists and shows progress while running. Errors render above the rows or the form in body color with retry; success is the toast plus an inline confirmation with a way back, since the expense leaves the queue. Titles: scene titles are the only headings; the card title is the amount and no heading repeats the button label.
